display.purpose: Cover masthead only; uppercase, negative right margin equal to tracking.

headline.purpose: Book title on the title page; uppercase.

title.purpose: Centred CHAPTER numeral in spaced capitals over a short double hairline; 1.05em of the column size.

section-head.purpose: Centred spaced-capital heads on frame pages with a 3rem hairline beneath.

body.purpose: Chapter text; size multiplied by --scale (0.8 to 1.5); measure --measure (26 to 46em, default 36em); face from --font.

note.purpose: Inline and focus notes; scaled with --scale.

note-margin.purpose: Notes in the open margin panels; scaled with --scale.

label.purpose: Running head, bar buttons, issue line, chapter navigation; always uppercase.

initial.purpose: Opening letter of a chapter, floated; first line continues in spaced capitals.

fontAssets.note: Reader-selectable column face only, not a system face.

rules.name: double-rule
rules.purpose: Thick-thin border between wrapper and page.

shadows.name: lifted-note
shadows.purpose: Hovered or pinned note raised over its neighbours in an open margin panel.

motion.name: column-shift
motion.purpose: Column slides aside when an open panel needs room.

layoutConstants.name: edge
layoutConstants.purpose: Panel to window edge; also page side gutter.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: ragged-right text, layer toggles on their own row, chapter crumb hidden, notes inline as footnotes.

components.description: Sticky buff wrapper bar on every page, closed by the thick-thin rule.
components.html: ScholiaLord Jim·Chapter I

components.name: Bar Button
components.description: Square hairline box in tracked capitals on the wrapper; inverts on hover.

components.name: Layer Toggle
components.description: Printer's mark in a square box: filled when the layer shows, hollow with the name struck through when off.

components.name: Segmented Control

components.name: Select

components.name: Stepper
components.description: Text size stepper: square hairline boxes that invert to ink on hover.
components.css: .ds-stepper { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .6rem; font-family: "Old Standard", "Century Schoolbook", Georgia, serif; color: var(--ink, #1c1a17); } .ds-stepper button { font: inherit; color: inherit; background: none; border: 1px solid var(--hair, #1c1a17); border-radius: 0; width: 2.6rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-stepper button:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--ink, #1c1a17); color: var(--ground, #f3f2ee); } .ds-stepper button:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--ink, #1c1a17); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-stepper button:disabled { opacity: .35; cursor: default; } .ds-stepper output { min-width: 3rem; text-align: center; }

narrative.overview:
Scholia is dressed as the Victorian literary magazine that first serialized these novels. The frame carries the period: a buff paper wrapper that owns the masthead and the running head, thick-thin rules where wrapper meets page, a contents page with dotted leaders, run-in capital heads, centred spaced-capital section heads. Inside that frame the reading column is plain book type on neutral newsprint, justified and hyphenated, indented paragraphs with no gap, a two-line initial opening each chapter. The period lives in the furniture, never in the paragraph.

The system is monochrome ink on paper. There is no colour accent: emphasis comes from weight, capitals, letterspacing, italic, and the printed hairline. One face, Old Standard TT, sets everything from masthead to margin note. Corners are square, rules are 1px ink, and depth is almost absent; a soft shadow appears only on things that genuinely float over the text (the settings card, a hovered or pinned margin note).

The signature is the scholarly apparatus: four printers' reference marks (* vocab, † allusion, § history, ¶ place) sit in the gutters level with each annotated line, and notes are set like a critical edition: mark, lemma in italic closed by a bracket, gloss, then source. The world rejects theme-park antique (parchment textures, seals, quills), the cream-paper and red-accent default, and app chrome (cards, pills, dashboards).
keyCharacteristics: Buff wrapper frame, neutral newsprint page, black ink, no hue accent.
Old Standard TT throughout; tracked uppercase for every frame label.
Square corners and 1px ink hairlines; thick-thin double rule as the frame border.
Printers' reference marks as the only iconography.
Book-set reading column: justified, hyphenated, indented, 36em measure by default.
Dark mode is a lamplit umber, not black.

rules.name: The No Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no hue accent. Emphasis is typographic (weight, capitals, italic, tracking) or a buff wash; never a red, blue, or any added colour.

rules.name: The Ink Rule Rule
rules.body: Every structural line is printed in the current ink at 1px (or the 3px+1px thick-thin pair). No grey dividers, no tinted borders.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Old Standard sets the whole frame. Reader font choices (EB Garamond, Georgia, Palatino, Charter, sans) apply only to the reading column and notes via `--font`; the frame always stays on `--frame`.

rules.name: The Run-In Rule
rules.body: Sub-heads inside prose are run-in bold spaced capitals (.82em, .08em tracking) leading the paragraph, not standalone headings.

rules.name: The Print Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest has a shadow. Shadows are soft and diffuse and appear only on an element that overlaps the text; never a hard offset shadow.

dos: Do frame every page with the buff wrapper and close it with the thick-thin rule in wrapper ink.
Do set frame labels in Old Standard uppercase, tracked .08em to .24em by rank.
Do draw every divider as a 1px ink hairline, square-cornered.
Do mark notes only with the four printers' marks: * vocab, † allusion, § history, ¶ place.
Do use Buff Wash for the active anchor and the hovered or pinned note.
Do keep the reading column at the reader's measure (36em default), indented paragraphs, justified and hyphenated only above 700px.
donts: Don't add a colour accent; no red, blue, or brand hue anywhere.
Don't round corners or use pill shapes; radius stays 0.
Don't wrap content in cards; the settings card is the only container.
Don't use parchment textures, wax seals, quills, or cream paper for the page ground.
Don't put shadows on resting elements or use hard offset shadows.
Don't introduce icon glyphs or icon fonts; the reference marks and drawn hairlines are the whole iconography.
Don't let the reader's font choice reach the frame; it changes the column and notes only.
